opening_activity: totaling a small stack of handwritten price tags on a hand-cranked mechanical adding machine when the crank abruptly locks halfway through a turn
opening_location: quiet indoor antiques market checkout counter near closing time
opening_environment: a narrow second-hand market counter surrounded by mismatched lamps, boxes, ceramics, and old household objects, with the mechanical adding machine centered in the host's working space
topic_visual_link: A hand-powered calculating machine visibly failing because of its interlocking gears creates a direct modern echo of the ancient geared mechanism later nicknamed a computer.
opening_visual_proof: the adding-machine crank is visibly frozen mid-turn while an exposed brass gear is wedged against the neighboring gear, leaving the number wheels stuck partway between positions
curiosity_trigger: the crank stops with a dry metallic catch, and the host notices the single jammed gear holding the entire calculating mechanism motionless
trigger_object: the jammed brass gear inside the hand-cranked adding machine
reaction: he gives the stuck gear a skeptical stare, lightly tests the crank once more, then tilts his head as the comparison clicks
entry_retrieval: after releasing the crank, he reaches to a nearby shelf beneath the counter, pulls out a topic-styled storybook, sets it beside the adding machine, and opens it
world_style_hint: dreamlike memory-collage imagery of corroded bronze fragments, nested gear trains, astronomical dials, moon phases, eclipse spirals, and a Mediterranean shipwreck
reason: A mundane hand-cranked calculator makes gears, computation, and mechanical failure immediately visible, giving the restrained host a natural reason to wonder how far back geared computing might go.
